Work_Details:
Around 2 years. 
I was in a SaaS company and work as UX designer to design interface for an app. The app is a social media management tool that can help companies manage different platforms all at one entry.
AI_Experiences: My coworker and I were talking about how AI could help shape the project management process, define the problem and suggest solutions. Then we discussed how hard it is to correctly and precisely define a problem. Even for PMs, it is a challenging job to collaborate with different parties to refine the original problem. So our conclusion was it is still impossible for AI to define the root problem but it is possible to provide more solutions and help explore ideas once a problem is well defined.
AI_Learning_Sources: Social media (TikTok, Twitter/X, YouTube, etc.),Conversations with peers or classmates
Future_Vision: Designers will be prompt engineer with ideas in mind but they do not need to have the skill to draw anymore
Top_Skill_Reason: This is the most human part I can think of. The empathy of different parties and communication style makes human different from AI tools.
Confidence_Reason: Professors hold different opinions of using AI in course work. Some really encourage us to try and benefit from AI, some even want to ban students from using AI. So the course design for AI-related education is still a gap in current curriculum.
Additional_Thoughts: AI can make design more efficient. But I doubt how creative AI can be if all the learning source are from existing artworks online.
